title: Login/request traffic can link parent identity to child account
description: Data in transit may contain identifiers, session parameters, URLs, or metadata that allow an observer or intermediary to link the parent's identity or account to a specific child account and grade request.
assumptions: The flow includes account identifiers, child selection information, or stable session metadata; transport metadata may be observable to network or infrastructure parties.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may vary; this is intended as a linking threat on the flow due to identifiers/metadata.

title: Parent or child may be identifiable from request metadata
description: Even if the payload is protected, request metadata such as IP address, device fingerprint, account name, or child-specific query parameters can identify the parent and indirectly identify the child whose grades are being requested.
assumptions: Infrastructure or intermediaries can observe metadata, or the application logs such metadata on receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id from memory for identifiability via observable metadata.

title: Portal may process the request for secondary purposes without parent awareness
description: On receipt of the login and grade request, the portal may use the parent's and child's data for analytics, profiling, monitoring, or other secondary purposes beyond authenticating and serving grades, without sufficiently informing the parent.
assumptions: The web app or connected services perform telemetry, profiling, or reuse of request data beyond the core service purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for unawareness/lack of transparency at the destination.

title: Portal may process parent-child account linkage without valid authorization basis
description: The destination may accept and process a parent's request for a child's grades without adequately verifying legal authority, custody status, school policy constraints, or age-related consent requirements, leading to non-compliant disclosure and processing.
assumptions: Authorization and policy checks may be incomplete or outdated, especially for changed guardianship situations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for non-compliance due to insufficient legal/policy basis checks.

title: Insufficient evidence of parent request or portal response
description: If the portal does not keep appropriate audit records of the parent's login and grade request, it may be difficult later to prove whether the parent requested access, whether access was authorized, or what child records were disclosed.
assumptions: Audit logging may be absent, incomplete, or not integrity-protected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for repudiation due to inadequate logging/evidence.

title: Portal stores or exposes more grade-related data than necessary
description: After receiving the request, the portal may retain detailed request contents, linked account data, or access history longer than necessary, or expose them internally to staff or subsystems that do not need them, increasing disclosure risk.
assumptions: The destination stores request logs, account linkage data, and access history beyond the minimum needed for service delivery and security.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subtree node may differ; this is a destination-side overexposure/overretention threat.

title: Excessive disclosure of student educational records to the parent
description: The portal may display more of the child's grades, teacher feedback, or submission history than is necessary for the parent's legitimate purpose, such as historical records, sensitive comments, or data from the wrong course or child. This creates a disclosure risk because the source process chooses what to reveal.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may aggregate and present detailed educational records and that not all displayed fields are strictly necessary for every parent interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on over-disclosure/minimisation concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Parent can identify sensitive performance details of the child
description: By presenting detailed grades, feedback, and submission history, the portal enables the parent to identify specific aspects of the child's academic performance, behavior, or difficulties. If the portal exposes records without adequate scoping or role checks, it may reveal highly specific and sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes educational performance data is privacy-sensitive and that identification risk is relevant when detailed records are exposed to a recipient.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent here because the child is known to the parent; this threat is mainly about revealing specific identifiable sensitive attributes, so the exact node mapping is approximate.

title: Linkability across courses, assignments, and time periods
description: The portal may combine grades, feedback, and submission history across multiple classes and time periods in one view, allowing the parent to link separate events and records into a richer profile of the child than intended.
assumptions: Assumes the UI aggregates records from multiple contexts rather than showing only a narrowly scoped item.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability through aggregation; exact subtree may differ.

title: Disclosure of educational records in transit
description: If the flow is not adequately protected in transit, grades, feedback, and submission history could be intercepted by network attackers or exposed through browser/network intermediaries, disclosing the child's educational records.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, caching controls, and endpoint security may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data disclosure during transfer; exact node id may differ depending on the threat tree variant used.

title: Linkability via communication metadata
description: Even if content is protected, metadata about repeated portal access and response sizes/timing may allow observers or intermediaries to link the parent to a particular student account or infer periods of academic activity such as grading events or submission deadlines.
assumptions: Assumes some observer can access traffic metadata, logs, or timing information.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for metadata-based linkability on the flow.

title: Further disclosure by the parent after receipt
description: Once the parent receives the child's grades, feedback, and submission history, they may intentionally or accidentally disclose it onward, for example by sharing screenshots, printing records, or discussing sensitive feedback with unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the destination is outside the system's direct control and may further share the data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for onward disclosure at the recipient; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Use of the child's educational data beyond the expected purpose
description: The parent may use the received educational records for purposes beyond the portal's intended educational-support context, such as punitive monitoring, sharing in family disputes, or retaining the data indefinitely. This creates a non-compliance/purpose-limitation risk at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation or policy expectations constrain how the data should be used after access.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance trees vary and downstream recipient misuse may be modeled differently.

title: Interception of administrator-submitted account and relationship data in transit
description: Names, emails, roles, account status changes, and parent-child relationship data sent from the School Administrator to the web app could be observed in transit by an unauthorized party, revealing personal data and administrative actions.
assumptions: Assumes the flow is not adequately protected end-to-end in transit, or that transport/session protections can be bypassed or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure/eavesdropping in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node labeling may vary.

title: Linkability via traffic metadata about account-management actions
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata on this flow may allow an observer to correlate when specific administrative events occur, such as creation, modification, disabling of accounts, or establishment of parent-child links, potentially linking affected individuals or households across events.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker can observe timing, frequency, endpoints, message sizes, or repeated patterns on the flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through communication metadata; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Identifiability of students, parents, or administrators from communication metadata
description: Observed metadata or partially exposed content on the flow could reveal which administrator is performing actions and which student/parent accounts or family relationships are being managed, making individuals identifiable even without full payload disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes metadata, identifiers in URLs, headers, or message patterns expose identity-related clues.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from metadata or exposed identifiers; exact node id may vary.

title: Excessive collection or retention of account and family-relationship data by the portal
description: On receipt, the Grades Portal Web App may store more personal data than necessary for account administration, or retain historical account states and parent-child links longer than needed, increasing privacy exposure for students, parents, and staff.
assumptions: Assumes the destination persists submitted data and may keep audit/history records beyond necessity.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data disclosure through over-collection/retention at the destination; exact node id may differ.

title: Linking family members and roles beyond what is necessary
description: The portal's processing of parent-child links together with names, emails, and roles can enable broad linkage of family relationships, student records, and administrative identities, potentially allowing profiling of households or role-based associations beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the destination combines this data with other portal records or exposes linked views internally.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by combining received data at the destination; exact node id may vary.

title: Unawareness of account-link changes affecting parents and students
description: Parents, students, or staff may be unaware that their accounts were created, modified, disabled, or linked to other individuals by an administrator, leaving them without clear notice of what data changed, why it changed, and what consequences follow.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not provide timely, understandable notices or status visibility to affected data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/awareness at the destination; exact node id may differ.

title: Processing account and relationship data without a valid legal basis or policy alignment
description: The portal may process names, emails, roles, account states, and parent-child relationships in ways that are not adequately justified by school policy, consent arrangements, contractual necessity, or other applicable legal basis, especially for sensitive family-link management.
assumptions: Assumes governance or legal-basis checks are insufficient or not enforced in the receiving system.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/legal-basis issues at the destination; exact node id may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence or contestability for administrative account changes
description: If the portal does not maintain trustworthy records of who created, modified, disabled accounts, or changed parent-child links, affected parties may be unable to prove or dispute actions taken on their data, undermining accountability and redress.
assumptions: Assumes logging, integrity protection, or user-visible history for administrative actions is weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability gaps at the destination; exact node id may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of account and family-link data to the directory
description: The grading service writes account records together with parent-child relationship links into the account directory. If the directory does not strictly need all attributes or relationship details for its purpose, P2's act of sharing can disclose more personal data than necessary, including sensitive household/family associations.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is used for account lookup/management and may not require full grading-context attributes or detailed relationship metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-effort at a generic disclosure-by-sharing level; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Linkability through centralized storage of parent-child relationships
description: By receiving and storing account records alongside explicit parent-child links, the account directory can link multiple identities into family units and correlate records across contexts. This can enable profiling of households and make separate accounts linkable through shared relationship data.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 can be queried or reused by other components, making stored relationship edges available for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic linkability node; exact subnode may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Identifiability of children and guardians from directory records
description: Account records combined with parent-child relationship links can directly identify a child via a known parent, or identify a parent via a known child. Even if some records are otherwise sparse, the relationship graph in DS3 can make individuals identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes account records contain names, usernames, emails, IDs, or other quasi-identifiers that become identifying when combined with family links.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate at a generic identifiability level.

title: Disclosure of family relationships from directory access or reuse
description: Once stored in the account directory, parent-child links may be exposed to internal services, administrators, or downstream consumers that only need basic account data. This reveals family relationships and potentially custody/guardian information beyond the original grading purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS3 is a shared datastore or is accessible to multiple roles/services.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for disclosure caused by recipient-side storage/reuse.

title: Unawareness of directory use for family-link storage
description: Data subjects may not expect the account directory to store and reuse parent-child relationship links originating from the grading service. If this secondary storage and use are not transparent, parents and children may be unaware of how their relationship data is processed.
assumptions: Assumes notices or UI do not clearly explain that grading-originated relationship data is written into DS3.
uncertainty_note: Generic unawareness node chosen; exact subnode may differ.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing unnecessary or over-retained relationship data
description: Persisting parent-child links and account records in the directory may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations if DS3 stores more relationship data than needed or keeps it longer than justified for account-directory purposes.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements impose minimization, purpose limitation, access control, and retention constraints.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate at a generic non-compliance level because no jurisdiction-specific control set was provided.

title: Linkability from flow metadata about relationship updates
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata on this flow—such as which account records are updated together, timing of writes, or repeated paired updates—can reveal that certain accounts are related as parent and child. This makes individuals linkable through transmission patterns.
assumptions: Assumes observers or logging systems can access traffic metadata or transaction traces for DF13.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node selection for linkability via data-flow metadata.

title: Oversharing of full grade, assignment, and directory data to third-party host
description: The source process sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory in nightly backups/replication to the cloud provider, which may disclose more personal data than is necessary for hosting or disaster recovery purposes.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider does not strictly require all fields or full historical records for the stated purpose, or less privacy-invasive backup patterns are feasible.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via unnecessary sharing/minimization failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Transfer to third-party cloud provider may be incompatible with original collection purpose or user expectations
description: Replicating student grades, assignments, and account-directory data to an external cloud hosting provider may exceed the purpose users reasonably expected when the data was collected, especially if notices or agreements did not clearly cover third-party hosting/replication.
assumptions: Users were not clearly informed that their educational records and directory data would be replicated to an external provider, or the transfer is broader than what was consented to or contractually authorized.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for purpose limitation/notice/consent concerns; exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Identification of students or staff from backup contents in transit
description: Because the replicated dataset contains full grade records and account-directory information, interception or exposure of the flow could directly identify individual students, instructors, or staff.
assumptions: The backup/replication stream is accessible to network, platform, or intermediary observers if transport protections fail or are misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identification node for direct identifiers present in transmitted content; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability of educational records with account-directory identities during transfer
description: The flow combines assignments, grades, and account-directory data in one replicated dataset, enabling records about performance and coursework to be linked to named accounts and potentially across courses or time periods.
assumptions: The transmitted backup preserves stable identifiers or account keys that connect educational records to directory identities.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node for combining datasets with stable identifiers; exact node id may vary.

title: Exposure of sensitive educational content and performance data in transit
description: Nightly shipment of full backups/replication may disclose confidential grades, assignment submissions, feedback, and directory details if the transfer channel, replication mechanism, or associated logs are exposed.
assumptions: Transport encryption, key management, endpoint authentication, or operational logging may be imperfect, creating a realistic exposure path.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for data in transit/logging exposure; exact node id may differ.

title: Cloud provider personnel or sub-processors may access replicated student records
description: Once received, the cloud hosting provider may process or store the replicated backups in ways that allow provider administrators, support staff, or sub-processors to access grades, assignments, and directory data beyond the controller's intended scope.
assumptions: Provider-side administrative access, support workflows, or subcontracting exist and are not fully constrained by technical and organizational controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure-at-destination node for recipient-side access; exact node id may differ.

title: Cloud provider can link replicated educational data across services, tenants, or time
description: At the destination, the provider may be able to correlate recurring nightly backups and account-directory identifiers to build longitudinal or cross-context linkages about individuals, even if hosting is the stated purpose.
assumptions: Provider systems retain stable identifiers, metadata, or operational telemetry that permit correlation across backup sets or environments.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability-at-recipient node; exact node id may differ.

title: Individuals may be unaware that their educational records are replicated to a third-party host
description: If the institution does not clearly communicate third-party backup/hosting arrangements, students and staff may be unaware that their grades, assignments, and directory data are stored and processed by an external provider.
assumptions: Privacy notices, contracts, or in-product explanations do not make this transfer sufficiently visible to affected individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for insufficient transparency about third-party hosting; exact node id may differ.

title: Provider retention, location, or secondary processing may violate policy or legal obligations
description: After receipt, the cloud provider may retain backups longer than permitted, replicate them to additional regions, or use sub-processors/secondary processing arrangements that conflict with educational-record obligations, contractual terms, or jurisdictional requirements.
assumptions: Provider-side retention schedules, geographic replication, or sub-processing are not fully aligned with the controller's legal and policy obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for retention/location/processor-governance issues; exact node id may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of grade records to the grading service
description: The grade records database may provide more student grade information than is necessary for the specific view being built, such as full historical records or records for unrelated students, parents, or teachers. This exposes personal educational data beyond the minimum needed for the task.
assumptions: The service may query broad record sets and the datastore may not enforce field-, row-, or purpose-based minimization.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on the catalog version.

title: Use of grade records for a broader purpose at the grading service
description: After receiving grade records, the assignment and grading service could process them for purposes beyond generating the intended student, parent, and teacher views, such as analytics, profiling, staff performance evaluation, or secondary reporting not expected by data subjects.
assumptions: P2 has access to raw grade records and may support multiple downstream features or administrative uses.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for secondary use/purpose creep.

title: Linkability of student, parent, and teacher records within the grading service
description: By combining grade records with role-specific view logic, the service can correlate students with parents, teachers, classes, and performance history. This may enable linking of records across contexts that data subjects did not expect to be connected.
assumptions: P2 has identifiers or relationship mappings that connect students, guardians, teachers, classes, and grades.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree for correlation/linking may differ by LINDDUN Pro edition.

title: Identifiability of individuals from grade records in the grading service
description: Even if some outputs are intended to be role-limited, the received grade records likely contain direct identifiers or quasi-identifiers that allow the service to identify specific students, parents, and teachers. This increases privacy risk if access controls or segregation are weak.
assumptions: Grade records include names, student IDs, class assignments, teacher associations, or similar identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from received personal data.

title: Identifiability via metadata on the database-to-service flow
description: Even if payload protections exist, metadata on the read flow—such as which records are requested, timing, frequency, class identifiers, or tenant/context identifiers—may reveal which student, parent, or teacher is being accessed or discussed.
assumptions: An observer of the flow or intermediary can access request/response metadata or traffic patterns.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; this is a metadata-based identifiability threat on the flow.

title: Linkability through repeated access patterns on the flow
description: Repeated queries from the grading service to the grade records database may allow an observer to correlate accesses over time, linking a sequence of grade-related events to the same student, class, teacher, or family relationship.
assumptions: Traffic analysis is possible and requests are distinguishable by identifiers, endpoints, or timing patterns.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; intended as a traffic-analysis/linkability threat.

title: Insufficient transparency to students, parents, and teachers about grade-record use
description: Data subjects may not be adequately informed that the grading service reads grade records to construct multiple role-based views, including what data is used, for which audiences, and under what access rules. This undermines awareness and informed expectations.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may not clearly describe this internal data use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Processing of educational records without an appropriate legal basis or policy alignment
description: The grading service's access to grade records for building student, parent, and teacher views may be non-compliant if role-based disclosures, parental access rules, retention, or educational privacy obligations are not properly enforced.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy rules constrain who may see grades and under what circumstances, especially for parent access and staff access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact compliance subtree depends on the governing regime and LINDDUN Pro version.
